title: OPSEC Ratings System & Coalition
description: A milestone-paid RFP with no application portal, multiple labelled deadlines, free-text eligibility and a service-agreement arrangement. Exercises every optional top-level field the standard defines: distinct sponsoring and operating organisations (each with its required slug), socialLinks as platform/url entries, the fundingInfo envelope, and the additionalReferences string.
summary: Milestone-paid RFP run by an operator on a sponsor's behalf.

sponsoringOrganizations.name: Example Foundation
sponsoringOrganizations.description: The issuing/backing entity. Not necessarily where the money comes from.

eligibility: stage: Teams with a shipped product and a public track record; geography: Global; jurisdiction: Excludes OFAC-sanctioned jurisdictions; entityType: Registered legal entity required before payout; compliance: KYB and quarterly reporting required
prerequisites: A proposal must include: prior track record, technical approach, a milestone plan with amounts, and disclosure of any conflicts.
additionalReferences: Original forum posting: https://forum.example.org/t/opsec-rfp/1 · Prior round retrospective: https://example.org/retro
serviceAgreement: Runs as a rolling ~12-month engagement rather than a one-off deliverable; renewal is decided at the end of each term by the sponsoring foundation.

milestones.title: Ratings framework published
milestones.criteria: Published methodology, reviewed by the coalition. Due within 8 weeks of kickoff.

milestones.title: Coalition assembled
milestones.criteria: At least five member organisations signed on.

milestones.title: First ratings round shipped
milestones.criteria: Ratings for twenty projects published with reproducible evidence.

deadlines.label: reviewed quarterly after the first round

fundingDetails.scope: Design, publish and operate an operational-security ratings system. In scope: methodology, coalition governance, first ratings round. Out of scope: custody of user funds, paid placement of any kind.
requirements: Methodology must be reproducible from public evidence.
All ratings must be published under an open licence.
